_about: Transiting planet over a natal point ('mars>venus'). Meanings rewritten in our own words. Main source: Sepharial, Astrology (1920), Sect. III ch. II 'The Effects of Transits' and Sect. II ch. IV 'Planetary Transits'; planet natures cross-checked with Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos I.5 and Lilly, Christian Astrology I. Pluto was found in 1930, after these books: its entries follow modern practice. The aspect decides which side shows: harmonious aspects lean to 'supportive', squares and oppositions to 'challenging', conjunctions to both. Sepharial: transits of the slow planets weigh most (Neptune, Uranus, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars in that order), they last longer when the planet is retrograde or stationary, and two planets on one point at once act more strongly.
